claim: Hell's Museum at Haw Par Villa stays open during the park's phased maintenance from Dec 2025, with free highlight tours.
quote: Hell's Museum, featuring the Ten Courts of Hell will remain open and visitors are welcome to experience the museum.

claim: The Ten Courts of Hell depicts sinners bludgeoned, chopped up and boiled in oil, traumatising 1970s-80s Singaporean kids.
quote: Topless sinners bludgeoned by demons, chopped up body parts, and people sizzling in oil woks terrorized a whole generation of Singaporean kids in the 70s and 80s.

claim: Haw Par Villa (formerly Tiger Balm Gardens) was built by the Tiger Balm Aw brothers; admission is free.
quote: Originally known as 'Tiger Balm Gardens,' it was created by brothers Aw Boon Haw and Aw Boon Par.

claim: Keppel Hill Reservoir is an abandoned colonial reservoir near Mount Faber, dubbed the forgotten reservoir.
quote: It's often dubbed as 'the forgotten reservoir', as it's disappeared off of modern maps until it was rediscovered a few years ago.

claim: The 1905 reservoir was used as a swimming pool by Japanese officers, vanished from maps by 1954, and was rediscovered in 2005 by a paranormal-investigation team.
quote: In 2005, the Asia Paranormal Investigators team led by Charles Goh came across an abandoned reservoir while they were searching for the lost tomb of a Japanese naval engineer.

claim: The trail to the reservoir passes the WWII Seah Im Bunker, an abandoned place in Singapore.
quote: The Defunct Keppel Hill Reservoir and Seah Im Bunker — Abandoned Places in Singapore

claim: The Rail Corridor is the official NParks greenway along the former railway line.
quote: National Parks Board Rail Corridor

claim: The Rail Corridor is a 24 km greenway created from the former Singapore-Kranji Railway that linked Singapore to Peninsular Malaysia.
quote: The Rail Corridor is a 24 kilometre-long greenway in Singapore created from sections of the former Singapore–Kranji Railway that once linked the island country to Peninsular Malaysia.

claim: A section of the Rail Corridor (South) is closed from 2 March 2026 for Phase 2 improvement works.
quote: FAQs Temporary Closure of Rail Corridor (South)

claim: Heritage guides run sunset walks through Bukit Brown Cemetery, whose main gate locks at 5:30PM.
quote: Spooky Singapore: Sunset at Bukit Brown Cemetery

claim: Bukit Brown has over 100,000 graves, strangler-fig Avatar trees, and tombs guarded by stone Sikh figures.
quote: Hiking Guide To Bukit Brown Cemetery & Avatar Trees

claim: Kampong Lorong Buangkok, built in 1956, is the last surviving kampong on mainland Singapore.
quote: Kampong Lorong Buangkok, built in 1956, is notable for being the last surviving kampong located in mainland Singapore.

claim: About 25 families still live in the kampong, whose land is worth ~SGD 70m, signed with obsolete 4-digit postcodes.
quote: Kampong Lorong Buangkok: Singapore's Last Village With 4-Digit Postal Code Street Signs

claim: Pulau Ubin has no mains electricity or running water; residents use diesel generators and well water.
quote: There's no electricity and running water here, so residents operate diesel generators for electricity and obtain their water supply from wells.

claim: About 38 residents still live on Pulau Ubin, the last witness of old kampung Singapore.
quote: About 38 residents still call the island home.

claim: The Battlebox is Singapore's only operational WWII bunker, built 1936-1939, where the Allies decided to surrender Singapore in Feb 1942.
quote: Built in 1936 and completed in 1939, the Battlebox served as the headquarters for the defending Allied forces against the invading Japanese army.

claim: Entry to the Battlebox is free but slot-limited and must be reserved in advance.
quote: Plan Your Visit | Historical World War II Bunker in Singapore | Battlebox

claim: The Tiong Bahru Air Raid Shelter is Singapore's only surviving pre-war civilian air raid shelter, with 19-inch-thick walls.
quote: The Tiong Bahru Air Raid Shelter is Singapore's only surviving pre-war civilian air raid shelter, built in the 1930s.

claim: The shelter is managed via heritage channels and opens only for special events and ROOTS tours.
quote: Tiong Bahru Air Raid Shelter

claim: From 19-26 Jan 2026 the shelter hosted Digital Art Week Asia's new-media exhibition '99 Years'.
quote: Digital Art Week Asia's New Media art exhibition '99 Years' comes to Tiong Bahru Air Raid Shelter

claim: MINT Museum of Toys holds over 50,000 vintage toys from the 1840s onward and the world's largest collection of Door of Hope dolls.
quote: MINT Museum of Toys houses the biggest collection of Door of Hope dolls in the world, handmade dolls designed and produced mostly in Shanghai by impoverished and abandoned girls.

claim: The MINT Museum of Toys is on Seah Street in the Bras Basah/Bugis precinct; tickets are SGD 25.
quote: Things To Do & Must-Visit Places in Singapore

claim: The Intan is an award-winning Peranakan home museum in Joo Chiat, viewable by appointment.
quote: The-Intan | My Rose Cut Diamond – An award winning Peranakan home museum

claim: Owner Alvin Yapp lives in The Intan among 5,000-plus Peranakan objects; visits are by appointment with tea.
quote: The Intan's curator and owner, Alvin Yapp, lives in the museum.

claim: Loyang Tua Pek Kong houses Taoist, Buddhist, Hindu and Malay Datuk Kong deities, with a Datuk shrine accessible only to those who have not eaten pork that day.
quote: a gravesite-shaped Datuk Gong shrine that is only accessible to individuals who have not consumed pork on the day of their visitation.

claim: Hajjah Fatimah Mosque, gazetted a national monument, has a famously leaning minaret.
quote: Hajjah Fatimah Mosque

claim: The mosque's minaret tilts about 6 degrees due to sandy foundations; it is the first local mosque named after a woman, fusing Islamic, European and Chinese design.
quote: Due to its sandy foundations, the mosque's minaret tilts about 6 degrees ... visitors have dubbed this unique fixture Singapore's very own Leaning Tower.

claim: Kusu Island ('Tortoise Island') has a temple to a turtle deity, Malay keramat shrines and a tortoise sanctuary.
quote: Tortoises of Kusu Island

claim: In the ninth lunar month thousands of devotees make pilgrimage to Kusu Island's Tua Pek Kong temple.
quote: Kusu Island - Singapore

claim: Singapore has many speakeasies hidden behind unmarked doors and disguised fronts.
quote: 13 Best Secret Bars In Singapore That Are Hidden From Sight

claim: Ume San 100 is hidden behind a row of vending machines and Mama Diam behind a shelf of vintage magazines.
quote: Ume San 100 - Hidden behind a row of unassuming vending machines ... Mama Diam - The entrance comes hidden behind a shelf lined with vintage knick-knacks.

claim: The Projector was an independent arthouse cinema founded in 2014 that closed in August 2025.
quote: The Projector was an independent cinema in Singapore founded in 2014 that specialized in arts-house films.

claim: Filmhouse, run by The Projector's former team, opened on 3 Feb 2026 in its old space at Golden Mile Tower with vintage audio gear.
quote: New indie cinema Filmhouse to take over The Projector at Golden Mile Tower

claim: Bizarre Singapore foods include claypot frog porridge and herbal turtle soup.
quote: 11 Bizarre Foods You Didn't Know You Could Find In Singapore

claim: Eminent Frog Porridge is a Michelin Bib Gourmand spot and Tan Ser Seng has served turtle soup since 1946.
quote: Tan Ser Seng Herbal Soup has been serving turtle herbal soup since 1946 ... Eminent Frog Porridge, a Michelin Bib Gourmand joint.

claim: Golden Mile and People's Park Complex are 1970s brutalist landmarks seen by some as eyesores.
quote: 7 Brutalist Buildings In Singapore To See Before They Are Gone

claim: The 16-storey Golden Mile Complex, likened to a typewriter, was designed as a self-contained vertical city and has been conserved.
quote: The 16-storey terraced Golden Mile Complex is often described as looking like a typewriter ... Designed as a self-contained 'vertical city'.

claim: The Toa Payoh Dragon Playground was built in 1979 with a terrazzo-tiled mosaic dragon by HDB architect Khor Ean Ghee.
quote: Toa Payoh Dragon Playground

claim: The Toa Payoh Lorong 6 dragon is the only one of its kind still standing in a sand-pit and is a popular Instagram landmark.
quote: The Toa Payoh Lorong 6 Dragon Playground is the only one that still stands in a sand-pit.

claim: Yip Yew Chong is a Singapore muralist whose works depict old everyday Singapore life.
quote: Art + Travel of YC

claim: Yip Yew Chong painted kampung-life murals in Everton Park, a neighbourhood of pre-war shophouses.
quote: The Everton Park murals are about village (or kampung) life in the old days of Singapore.

claim: Gelam Gallery is Singapore's first outdoor gallery, with over 30 artworks in the back lanes of Muscat Street, open 24/7 and free.
quote: Gelam Gallery is tucked away in the back alleys of Muscat Street and is Singapore's first outdoor art gallery ... Over 30 artworks occupy this space.

claim: Sembawang Hot Spring Park is the official NParks site of Singapore's only natural hot spring.
quote: Sembawang Hot Spring Park

claim: Sembawang is Singapore's only natural hot spring, flowing for locals since as early as 1908.
quote: The Sembawang Hot Spring Park was a naturally occurring anomaly providing actual hot spring water to locals as early as 1908.

claim: Visitors collect 70°C hot spring water in buckets to cook eggs at an egg-cooking station.
quote: Visitors can collect hot spring water at 70°C in their own buckets or cook eggs using the hot spring water at the egg cooking station.

claim: Thow Kwang Pottery Jungle is the official site of the dragon kiln, offering crafts and workshops.
quote: Thow Kwang Pottery Jungle | Dragon kiln, Crafts & Workshops!

claim: Thow Kwang has the oldest surviving dragon kiln, a 27-metre wood-fired tunnel fired two to three times a year for spectators.
quote: The 27-meter-long kiln is built at a steep slope ... the Tan family fires up the dragon two to three times each year.

claim: Hay Dairies is Singapore's only goat farm (800+ goats), with daily 9am milking sessions, in the Kranji countryside.
quote: Attractions - Singapore

claim: Bollywood Veggies is a 10-acre pesticide-free vegetable farm launched by Ivy Singh-Lim in 2000.
quote: It is a 10-acre vegetable farm that was launched by Ivy Singh-Lim and Lim Ho Seng in the year 2000.

claim: Lazarus Island is a quiet, near-empty white-sand beach connected to St John's Island by causeway.
quote: St John's and Lazarus Island: Singapore's Hidden Beach Getaway

claim: The Southern Islands including Lazarus and St John's are state-managed and reached by ferry.
quote: Visiting the SLA-Managed Islands | Singapore Land Authority

claim: The Southern Ridges is a 10 km trail via Henderson Waves, Singapore's highest pedestrian bridge at 36m of curved steel and Balau wood.
quote: Henderson Waves ... is Singapore's highest pedestrian bridge standing 36 meters above Henderson Road.

claim: Geylang is a layered, unsanitised neighbourhood of red-light lorongs, temples and conservation shophouses.
quote: Beyond the Red Light: Geylang and Its Storied Lorongs

claim: Geylang mixes the red-light district with temples, Peranakan shophouses and round-the-clock hawkers serving frog porridge and pig-organ soup.
quote: Juxtaposed against the red light district are places of worship, conservation-status Peranakan shophouses, long-standing heritage restaurants and hawkers.

claim: Gillman Barracks is a 1930s army camp the British handed to Singapore for SGD 1, relaunched as a contemporary-art enclave in 2012.
quote: the British handed over Gillman Barracks to the Singapore Armed Forces (SAF) for a token sum of $1 ... launched in September 2012 as a contemporary art centre.

claim: Gillman Barracks is an art cluster of galleries, cafes and bars in old barrack buildings.
quote: Gillman Barracks guide: The coolest galleries, cafes, and bars in this funky art cluster

claim: Sungei Road's Thieves' Market was Singapore's largest, oldest flea market from the 1930s, closed permanently in July 2017.
quote: The market was permanently closed on 10 July 2017 for 'future residential development use'.

claim: The Thieves' Market traded second-hand and contraband goods, with 200-plus peddlers at its 1950s peak.
quote: Sungei Road Thieves Market in Singapore
